newsitem.title: INDIA: India's new president calls for war on corruption.
newsitem.headline: India's new president calls for war on corruption.

text.p: Kocheril Raman Narayanan took office on Friday as India's 10th president, becoming the first member of a low Hindu caste to be elected to the highest office of the world's largest democracy.

In his first speech after a swearing-in ceremony at New Delhi's Parliament House, the 76-year-old leader said he wanted Indians to unite in a fight against what independence leader Mahatma Gandhi called "the demon of corruption".
Narayanan, a former diplomat who was born into a poor southern Indian family, was elected last week to succeed Shankar Dayal Sharma, whose five-year term ended on Friday.
His rise to the position of India's head of state is seen as a symbol of triumph for low castes struggling for empowerment to undo centuries of discrimination under the Hindu social hierarchy.

"Today there are signs of a weakening of the moral and spiritual fibre in our public life with the evils of communalism, casteism, violence and corruption bedevilling our society," Narayanan said after he was sworn in.

His remarks come in the midst of a national debate on corruption sparked by a $280 million scandal which has rattled Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's minority coalition, formed after elections last year to oust Hindu nationalists from power.
The president, India's constitutional head, is traditionally seen as a figurehead but is considered crucial with the emergence of coalition politics since he plays a key role in government formation.
"Excessive obsession with the pursuit of pure politics has often overshadowed the social, economic and developmental needs of the people," Narayanan said.
Narayanan's candidature was backed by India's three main political groups -- the ruling United Front, its vital ally the Congress party, and the main opposition Hindu Bharatiya Party.
